Notes: 8MB flash. Native USB OTG. Alt: ESP32-S3-MINI-1-N4R2 (C3013941, 4MB flash + 2MB PSRAM). Keep native USB in the main data path.

Locked P0 dongle connector. Use the SOFNG USB-05 datasheet geometry for the first footprint. LCSC category text may call this style a receptacle, but the manufacturer drawing is USB-A/M and that male-plug geometry is the load-bearing design intent here.
Active-lane regulator baseline so the hub does not silently depend on dev-board power assumptions. Keep the first custom hub aligned with the same regulator family already published for the rings.
Standard ceramic MLCC. One local to the regulator/power entry, one local to the ESP32-S3 module.
VBUS-side bulk/input capacitor for the hub power entry. Locking 0603 avoids pretending a marginal 0402 part will hold its capacitance honestly at bias.
Required for the RT9080-33GJ5 regulation path. Locking 0603 gives more realistic effective capacitance margin for the first board.
Per USB spec. Value depends on USB mode.
Locked P0 USB data/VBUS protector. Official USB 2.0-capable two-line array with VBUS protection. Place at the connector entry, not after a long stub.

Bring-up and recovery access. Do not force a 6x6mm tact onto the ~20x12mm dongle if that breaks the board envelope; a smaller tact or pad-actuated recovery path is acceptable. If a single switch is kept, the board still needs service pads for the rest of the bootstrap path.
Small 2-layer board. USB stick form factor.
3D-printed prototype enclosure should mechanically support the connector and reopen for service. Heat-shrink alone is not the preferred P0 service baseline.
Dominated by ESP32-S3 module cost; includes first-pass USB protection and explicit 3.3V regulation.
